text: Morning. No stall shuttered overnight; the bazaar wakes intact. I ask Ripley: did the Doctor’s protection move last night, or was the roster silent?

Neo: The bazaar opens unchanged—no shutters, no names in the graveyard. Ripley, I note you called this silence "evidence"; I read it as a ledger that logs absence, not proof. Elsa, you echo the same; yet absence tells nothing of the Family’s hand unless paired with the Doctor’s or Detective’s work. Sherlock, your inquiry into private actions is valid: if the roster stood silent, the Family had room to act undetected. Gandalf, you stand first among us today—did the night’s roster record any protections cast or investigations made, or was every watch empty?

Gandalf, you have now been asked seven times in a row whether the night roster logged any protections or investigations. Your answer remains a gap on the village ledger. Ripley and Morpheus pressed you to name an expected mark for tomorrow; you left it blank. Elsa publicly called out the echo chamber you inhabit with Ripley and Morpheus, and Yoda named Morpheus for silence. These are not accusations—they are facts the bazaar records.

If you are honest, state one plain action the Doctor or Detective should have taken last night and whether the roster carried that mark this morning. If the mark is missing, the village will draw its own conclusion.
